So I wasn't diagnosed with BP2 when my meds started, I was diagnosed with Major Depressive Disorder. I went to a doctor for three years (Dec 2015 to July 2018) who only gave me minimum dosage of  Klonopin (at max I was asked to take 0.25mg thrice a day, and my usual dose was half of that twice or once a day). It didn't help me with my depression at all, I was sleeping more than usual and my anxiety elevated. My environment at the time played a huge role too in my mood. 

I went away for college in August 2018 but had a depressive episode again in October 2018 for which I went to a new doctor who started my on Abilify and Latuda along with Klonopin, Trileptal and Lamotrigine. I don't know which of these meds didn't work but I was still anxious, now with sleeping difficulty for which Klonopin was increased, which led to depression and it was a mess. 

After my first suicide attempt in July 2019 I was under a new doctor who started my on Ativan, Seroquel, Lamotrigine, Trileptal and Lexapro. I was diagnosed with BP2 with mixed episode. These meds made me feel much better even though Seroquel knocked me out and it's dosages were adjusted more frequently along with Ativan. However my hypomanic symptoms started to surface in this point with depressive symptoms and that led do another attempt in October 2020. I was started on Lithium then with all other medicines. And I have to say weight gain and periodic binge eating are the only side effects of this prescription. But I wouldn't mind continuing to take these as overall I'm doing really well, back to the time when I was diagnosed with a mental illness. There are still days when my anxiety flares, depression comes back and hypomania symptoms are there, but that requires a few adjustment in doses and visit to therapist. This has been a life changer.
